## What I did

- Located the file: `1UBQ.pdb` at the root of workspace **Mors Lab** (`00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`). `smarts_read_file` confirmed the key is valid and returned 970 lines (~79 KB) — consistent with 1UBQ (76-residue ubiquitin, 660 atoms plus header/REMARK block).
- Tried `smarts_analyze_file` (structure analysis, which reports method/resolution/chains/B-factor) three times, including with `viewer_type: "structure"`. It failed every time with `Analysis failed: Failed to get file URL`. So I did **not** read the method and resolution out of the file's own `EXPDTA` / `REMARK 2` lines — the full file text exceeded my output limit and I have no grep/read tool for the saved dump in this session.
- Instead I looked up the entry in the PDB with `smarts_run_tool` → `pdb-toolkit`, `operation: metadata`, `pdb_id: 1UBQ`.

## Provenance and caveat

The values below come from the **RCSB PDB entry 1UBQ** (https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1UBQ), not from parsing your local copy. The entry title — "STRUCTURE OF UBIQUITIN REFINED AT 1.8 ANGSTROMS RESOLUTION" (Vijay-Kumar, Bugg & Cook, deposited 1987-04-16) — carries the resolution internally, which is a good cross-check. This is a database lookup, not a prediction, so there is no confidence score; the only assumption is that your `1UBQ.pdb` is the unmodified PDB entry rather than a re-refined or edited variant. If you want it verified against the file itself, the structure analyzer needs to be fixed first (that "Failed to get file URL" error looks like a bio-analytics/presigned-URL issue, not a bad key, since `smarts_read_file` resolved the same key fine).

Also from the same record: space group P 2₁ 2₁ 2₁, classification "chromosomal protein", 1 polymer entity.

## ANSWER

- **Experimental method:** X-ray diffraction (X-ray crystallography)
- **Resolution:** 1.8 Å
